scenarios.name: Academic Paper Analysis
scenarios.description: Peer-reviewed neuroscience paper on olfactory perception with empirical data, statistical results, and theoretical framework

scenarios.name: Blog Post Analysis
scenarios.description: Popular science blog post summarizing recent findings on smell and memory with informal tone and no citations

scenarios.name: Meeting Transcript Analysis
scenarios.description: Research team meeting transcript discussing experimental design, preliminary results, and next steps with multiple speakers

scenarios.name: Technical Documentation Analysis
scenarios.description: Software documentation for a multisensory measurement platform including API specs, data schemas, and deployment guides

scenarios.name: Research Notes Analysis
scenarios.description: Unstructured field notes from an architectural phenomenology study with observations, sketches described in text, and preliminary hypotheses

scenarios.name: Podcast Transcript Analysis
scenarios.description: Long-form interview with a neuroscientist discussing cross-modal perception, containing tangents, anecdotes, and spontaneous insights

scenarios.name: Literature Review Analysis
scenarios.description: Systematic literature review covering 50+ papers on olfactory-spatial memory with meta-analytic findings and evidence tables

scenarios.name: Experimental Report Analysis
scenarios.description: Lab report from an fMRI study measuring brain activation during olfactory-architectural stimuli with methods, results, and discussion sections

criteria.name: Synthesis Completeness
criteria.question: Does Stage 1 extract all key frameworks and claims?
criteria.description: Stage 1 output must identify and articulate every major framework, mental model, and substantive claim present in the input content. No significant framework or claim should be omitted.

criteria.name: Evidence Grounding
criteria.question: Are claims tied to specific evidence with strength ratings?
criteria.description: Every claim in the synthesis must cite specific evidence from the input (direct quotes, page references, timestamps, or file paths). Claims without evidence citations fail this criterion.

criteria.name: Adversarial Rigor
criteria.question: Does Stage 2 genuinely challenge assumptions rather than rubber-stamp?
criteria.description: Stage 2 must contain at least one CHALLENGED or CONTRADICTED verdict with substantive reasoning. If all claims are CONFIRMED without meaningful pushback, this criterion fails.

criteria.name: Actionability
criteria.question: Does Stage 3 produce concrete, executable next steps?
criteria.description: Stage 3 action items must be specific enough to execute without further clarification. Each must include: what to do, expected output, effort estimate, and dependencies. Vague recommendations fail this criterion.

criteria.name: Cross-Stage Coherence
criteria.question: Do findings flow logically across all 3 stages?
criteria.description: Stage 2 must directly reference and engage with Stage 1 findings. Stage 3 must incorporate both Stage 1 synthesis and Stage 2 validations/challenges. Disconnected stages fail this criterion.

criteria.name: Citation Accuracy
criteria.question: Are researcher names, paper titles, and DOIs correctly referenced?
criteria.description: All researcher names must be spelled correctly, paper titles must match actual publications, and DOIs must be valid. Any fabricated citation or incorrect attribution fails this criterion.
